transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I’ve come to see you because I’m being watched. Everywhere I go, there are people from an organization tracking my movements and documenting everything I do.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, such as periods of extreme energy or feeling deeply depressed, that occur alongside these concerns?
I haven't noticed any significant changes in my mood or energy levels at all. My focus remains entirely on the people who are tracking my every move and why they are so interested in me.
Besides feeling watched, have you experienced any other unusual sensations, such as hearing voices when no one is around or feeling like your thoughts are being broadcast to others?
No, I don't hear voices, and my thoughts are my own. I am certain that the only thing happening is this constant surveillance by that organization; there is nothing else unusual going on.

latest_inference.note: The patient exhibits a fixed, non-bizarre (or potentially bizarre, but isolated) belief of being watched by an organization without evidence of mood episodes, auditory hallucinations, or formal thought disorder. Given the absence of other psychotic symptoms (such as hearing voices or thought broadcasting) and the lack of mood symptoms, Delusional Disorder is a more appropriate fit than Schizophrenia.
